messages:
ashwin: Quick ask — compiling vendor pricing inputs for our Q3 cost model. Need: spot tiers (per GPU/hr), 1yr/3yr reserved monthly equivalents, minimum commit sizes, expected preemption rates, marketplace SKU IDs, and any discount stacking rules. Drop numbers/links here by EOD Wed.

sarah: TL;DR — single sheet we can import into the model would be ideal (CSV/Google Sheet). Columns: partner, region, sku, spot$, reserve_1yr$, reserve_3yr$, commit_min, preempt_rate, notes.

ben: Pasting what partners shared in the last sync. these are partner-provided public numbers (untested). I added a short notes column for assumptions.

ben: ```
partner,region,sku,spot_usd_per_gpu_hr,reserve_1yr_usd_per_gpu_month,reserve_3yr_usd_per_gpu_month,commit_min_gpus,preempt_rate,notes
Velox,us-west1,velox.a100x_v3,0.22,1200,900,4,0.05,baseline pricing; includes basic network
Astra,us-east1,astra.a100x_v3,0.18,1100,850,8,0.12,lower spot but higher preempt in peak
Nimbus,eu-west1,nimbus.h100_v2,0.26,1300,1000,2,0.03,premium HW; limited inventory windows
```

carmen: Two quick operational notes: (1) Velox reserve quoted assumes a 2-week lead for capacity ramping during commit term; (2) Astra spot preempt is heavily correlated with EU business hours — expect spikes Mon-Fri 09-18 CET.

jordan: Marketplace/partner-comms note — Velox allows stacking our marketplace credit up to 20% on reserve SKUs, but not on spot. Astra disallows any third-party credits on reserved SKUs (they require direct contract). We should model both scenarios.

marketplace-bot: Velox marketplace: price adjustment alert — spot +5% in us-west1 effective 2026-03-10. See https://partners.velox/status/2345

ashwin: @sarah @ben can you (1) reconcile these into the canonical sheet and (2) add a conservative fallback price for modeling (velox +15% vs current spot) to simulate supply shocks?

ben: Yep — I uploaded a CSV to the partnerships drive: https://drive.redwood/partnerships/q3-hw-pricing.csv. Fallback assumptions I added: fallback_multiplier = 1.15 for immediate shock, 1.35 for sustained 2-week outage. Also added a small sensitivity column for quantization changes (we assume 10% fewer GPUs needed -> lowers effective cost).

ashwin: Carmen — any rough windows on when partner-committed reserved capacity becomes deliverable? we need lead times for ramp modeling.

carmen: Velox: 2w after contract; Astra: 4-6w for >32 GPU commits (they spin up nodes), Nimbus: requires proof-of-usage and can take 6-8w for large EU orders. I'll request explicit calendar dates from each partner.

ashwin: Perfect. Also callout: include any cancellation/early-termination fees so finance can amortize.

ben: added early-term row: Velox = 25% of remaining term, Astra = pro-rata with 30d notice penalty, Nimbus = case-by-case.

sarah: For the model, I'll add these fields: cancel_fee_type, cancel_fee_pct_or_terms, ramp_weeks, credit_stack_allowed (yes/no), marketplace_sku_link. I'll push the sheet by EOD Wed and tag folks.

jordan: One more: for joint announcements / marketplace launches, partners sometimes give promo credits for first 3 months — if available, mark as "promo_credit_usd" in sheet so we can simulate net-first-year costs.

ashwin: Great capture. Final asks: everyone drop final verified numbers and links by EOD Wed; mark anything still tentative with "TENTATIVE" in notes. We'll run the baseline vs shock scenarios Thu morning. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
